lines.text: There's a loading bar across the sky. Tonight it hit *99 percent.*
It showed up on a Tuesday. A thin white line, from one side of the sky to the other. Everyone on Earth could see it.
Under it, one word. *Updating.* One percent.
Planes flew right through it. Telescopes couldn't focus on it. It was always the same distance away. Like a crack in a *screen.*
It went up one percent a day. After a week, people got used to it. They made memes.
At 50 percent, a few stars moved. Just a few. Like someone *rearranging the furniture.*
At 80, the birds stopped flying. They sat on every wire in the world, all facing the bar. *Waiting.*
Tonight it hit 99. And it stopped.
A box opened in the sky, bigger than the moon. *Restart required.* Two buttons. *Now.* Or *tonight.*
Everyone on Earth looked up at the same time. Nobody knew who was supposed to click.
Then a cursor appeared. A little white arrow, the size of a city.
It drifted across the sky. Over the oceans. Over the cities. Slowly. Like it was *looking* for someone.
It stopped over my town. Over my street. Over *my house.*
Then my phone lit up. One notification. *You choose.*
